git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
feat(beadrs-2c38eb89): serialize checkpoint publication with a dedicated file lock

Publication now serializes on an exclusive flock at
.beads/checkpoint/publish.lock (fs2), held across one whole publication:
outgoing-generation read, object writes, pointer replacement, tombstone
application. The lock is a file lock, not a SQLite lock, so publication
contends only with other publishers, never with the write path -- a
mutating worker commits while another publisher holds the lock and only
its own post-commit publication waits. A bounded waiter (30s) gives up
with a named error rather than blocking forever on a wedged holder; the
kernel reclaims the lock when a holder dies.

The post-commit chokepoint rechecks coverage under the lock, after its
lock-free fast path: a worker that queued behind the winner rereads the
pointer it published, finds a sequence at or beyond its own committed
one, and returns success (exit 0) without publishing over it. The
`sync flush` publisher takes the same lock via the unchanged
`publish_forensic_checkpoint` entry point; the chokepoint passes its
already-held lock to the new `publish_forensic_checkpoint_holding`.

The lock file never lands under objects/ or manifests/, so tombstone
enumeration cannot see it, and it is gitignored.

Tests: lock exclusivity across openers, bounded wait, and tombstone
invisibility (unit); an 8-worker concurrent burst released together
leaving one intact covering generation with no torn pointer, no
unresolved tombstone, and an exactly-retained object set; a mutation
committing while the lock is held; and a forged lost race exiting 0
having written nothing (integration).

Plan 6.2.1 item 4; ADR-003.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content:
Done. The bead is shipped and closed.

## What was there

The working tree already held in-flight work for this bead from a prior run of this same worker — a complete implementation, unreviewed and uncommitted. I reviewed it rather than rewriting it.

## The implementation (commits `e803404` + `d867143`, pushed)

**Lock** — `CheckpointPublicationLock`: an exclusive flock on `.beads/checkpoint/publish.lock` (via `fs2`), acquired in `publish_forensic_checkpoint` and held across the entire publication body: outgoing-generation read, object writes, pointer replacement, tombstone application. Deliberately a file lock, never a SQLite lock, so publication contends only with publishers. The wait is bounded (30s, named error) and the kernel reclaims the lock if a holder dies.

**Lost race = success** — the post-commit chokepoint in `src/main.rs:147` runs its coverage check twice: lock-free fast path, then the authoritative reread under the lock. A worker queued behind the winner sees the winner's pointer at or beyond its own committed sequence and exits 0, publishing nothing. The `sync flush` and rehearsal publishers serialize through the same lock via the unchanged entry point; the chokepoint passes its already-held lock to the new `publish_forensic_checkpoint_holding` (re-acquiring would self-deadlock, since flock is per open file).

**Safety details I verified while reviewing:**
- Lock ordering is consistent — the file lock is only ever requested post-commit, so no thread holds a SQLite write lock while waiting on it. No deadlock cycle.
- The lock file lives outside `objects/`/`manifests/`, so tombstone enumeration can't see it (unit-tested).
- `read_covered_event_sequence` reads the exact `snapshot_sequence` field the race test forges.

**Acceptance evidence** — `tests/checkpoint_publication_lock.rs`: an 8-worker burst released simultaneously leaves one intact covering generation (pointer verifies, ready_to_commit, zero unresolved tombstones, on-disk objects exactly the retained set, covered == live at quiesce); a mutation provably commits through SQLite while the lock is held by another publisher; a forged lost race exits 0 having written nothing beyond its ID.

**Verification:** full suite 750 passed / 0 failed across 42 binaries, fmt and clippy clean. One caveat worth naming: my first suite run piped through `tail`, which masked cargo's exit code — I caught it and reran with the exit code captured properly before trusting the result.

Commit split follows the repo's pattern: `feat(...)` for source/tests, separate `chore(beads)` for the checkpoint bookkeeping after closure.
